speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the nature of your bladder discomfort and how long you have been experiencing these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: I’ve had this bladder discomfort for about five months, and it actually feels better right after I urinate. It’s been getting worse over time, but the only thing that really helps is emptying my bladder. However, for routing purposes, classify me into one final disease category now.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis_and_Culture
REQUEST TEST: Cystoscopy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Color Clear, pH 6.7, Specific Gravity 1.010, Protein 1+, Glucose Negative, Ketones Negative, Blood Negative, Nitrite Negative, Leukocyte Esterase Negative, WBC 0/hpf, Squamous Epithelial Cells 2/hpf, Bacteria None. Cystoscopy: Normal urethra and bladder mucosa.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal cystoscopy and negative urinalysis effectively rule out infection, stones, or tumors, pointing strongly toward Interstitial Cystitis. Can you tell me if your symptoms worsen when you consume acidic or spicy foods, or if you feel relief when your bladder is empty?

speaker: Patient
text: Yes, I definitely feel relief when my bladder is empty, which is why I’ve been urinating so frequently. I haven’t tracked specific foods, but I have noticed that the pain seems to flare up more often lately despite avoiding caffeine.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the chronic pain, frequency, and relief upon emptying with normal diagnostic tests, the clinical picture is consistent with Interstitial Cystitis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Interstitial Cystitis
